title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet:
Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard -  Dark Souls - item - trivia 
 trivia : The Japanese description of Seath's Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard uses the term (Hepburn: *gaiseki*) 'consort kin', which is used to define a person related by marriage to the maternal clan or wife's clan of the monarch, thus stating how Seath had become part of Gwyn's family through marriage with one of the daughters of his mother. However, if interpreted differently by reading the individual kanji separately like 外 (Gai) and 戚 (Seki), it would be translated as "external relative", implying that Seath would have married any woman from Gwyn's family.

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard
snippet: **While the term has a historical and cultural meaning too complex to properly convey in the context of the game's lore and the fact that one could become a "Gaiseki" even marrying a sibling or cousin of the monarch's mother or even by having the monarch marry one's daughter, it is more likely that Gwyn gave Seath one of his daughters as a gift thus allowing the dragon a more close connection to the family of the monarch.

title: Darklurker
snippet:
Darklurker -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : The Darklurker is weak to Lightning and has moderate Fire and Magic resistance. It's extremely resistant to Dark damage. A high elemental defense, especially against Fire and Dark, is very effective, as the Darklurker deals no physical damage. A shield with overall high elemental defenses and stability, such as the Rebel's Greatshield, can greatly reduce damage taken from many of its attacks.

Once the Darklurker's health drops below 60%, it will attempt to make a copy of itself, telegraphed by it creating a bright light and folding its wings around itself. During this phase, it can be staggered to postpone the split. An effective spell to use during this phase would be an area-of-effect pyromancy spell, such as Flame Swathe or Chaos Storm, as both of the Darklurkers will take massive fire damage if they are caught in the blast.

title: Darklurker
snippet:
Darklurker -  Dark Souls II - boss - attacks 
 attacks : **Dark Sword**: The Darklurker raises its left hand to its right shoulder, materializing a white energy blade that it will then swing at the player. Has a relatively long delay compared to melee attacks by most other enemies, so be prepared to roll later rather than earlier to avoid. This attack deals Dark damage and can swing up to two times in a row. The swings can also be followed up with a stab.

**Laser Beam**: The Darklurker flaps its wings and floats above the arena, firing off a bright, slow-moving beam of Dark after a short delay. Has some tracking and can deal tremendous damage if it hits, but cannot hit targets that are directly below it. While it is best to keep moving to avoid the beam, the Darklurker is vulnerable to ranged attacks and spells while firing the beam.

title: Darklurker
snippet:
Darklurker -  Dark Souls II - boss - general_information 
 general_information : The Darklurker can be fought only through the Pilgrims of Dark covenant. The player will be transported to its arena once all beacons in the Dark Chasm of Old are lit and all three dungeons have been cleared. In order to access this boss, one must simply clear a chasm as normal once all of the conditions are met. This may be jarring, as the player may end up fighting it unprepared upon lighting the third beacon and clearing the third chasm.

It appears as a four-armed angelic humanoid, with its face completely obscured by a hood. Its lower arms are constantly folded across its chest.

title: Darklurker
snippet:
**Explosion**: The Darklurker gathers its arms together and leans backward. It then creates an explosion in a wide area around it, dealing heavy damage. The area is somewhat wider in front of it.

**Split**: When the Darklurker reaches around 60% health, it will cross all of its arms around itself, fold its wings in, and a purple cloud will appear around it and focus in. The Darklurker will then split into two; it is vulnerable to attacks during and shortly after this spell. Both share the boss's HP and must be fought at once as the fight goes on. The copy is identical to the original, and both can use any of the Darklurker's attacks and spells at any time. Note that while this move can be stopped through staggering, the time window for doing so is extremely small as the move only takes about two to three seconds.

title: Darklurker
snippet:
**Dark Spear**: Raises its left arm into the air to point straight up, then fires a Dark bolt that resembles a Soul Spear. Has relatively poor tracking and can be easily dodged by rolling, but has a very small delay and can catch unprepared players by surprise.

**Dark Meteor**: The Darklurker will raise its right arm and point upward. A black portal will appear above the Darklurker and another will appear somewhere else in the arena. The Darklurker will send a dark orb into the portal above it, which will then emerge from the other portal and fly toward the player, exploding in a moderate sized area of effect. Has moderate homing, so jumping on top of rolling may be necessary to avoid.

**Fire Balls**: Raises all four arms into the air, creating a large orange orb above it, then launches three fireballs from it after a delay. Has no tracking and can be avoided by running to the side.

Seath's character is an homage to the dragon god of the same name in FromSoftware's King's Field series for the original Playstation. The Souls series is often referred to as the spiritual successor to King's Field.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - strategies

Loss of souls and humanity can be avoided by wearing a Ring of Sacrifice, but if he kills the player through Curse, then a Rare Ring of Sacrifice is needed to avoid penalties. title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath eventually sired a humanoid hybrid daughter, Shira. Although the mother is never stated explicitly, Shira is both "one whose veins coarse with royal blood", and a "descendant of Gods", making her likely mother Seath's spouse who was a relative of Gwyn.
 Shira became the sworn knight and personal handmaiden to Princess Filianore, Gwyn's last daughter, and the two, together with the dragon Darkeater Midir, would be forever sent away to the Ringed City, the hidden city Gwyn gifted to the humans who helped him end the Age of Ancients, so that the three would keep the Dark within at bay. Shira would remain in the Ringed City for the rest of her life, dutifully guarding Filianore over countless ages, although she would always take pride in being Seath's daughter.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Another possible daughter of Seath was Crossbreed Priscilla, a half-dragon hybrid whose dragon attributes are reminiscent of him; as she is outright described as a bastard, she would have been conceived out of wedlock. Priscilla was feared by the other gods and treated as an abomination due to her Lifehunt powers and unnatural origin. Eventually she was drawn away into the cold and lonely Painted World of Ariamis, trapped within a great canvas.

Seath seemingly had little interest in politics or pleasure, choosing to immerse himself in research of the scales of immortality that the ancient dragons possessed but he lacked. His Archives became a magnificent pool of tomes and knowledge, the fruits of Seath's superior wisdom and unsound fixation over achieving the immortality that was denied to him at birth.

He was instrumental in the gods' eventual victory, and the triumphant Lords would exterminate much of the Ancient Dragons, cementing their rule. title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Following the death of their creator, multiple moon butterflies survived over the centuries, migrating to Drangleic and mutating into lesser Great Moths and developing poisoning abilities. title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Studying the sorceries and knowledge brought to the Archives by the Crystal Sages, Oceiros would find himself walking the same path as Big Hat Logan, one that led to enlightenment only to be followed by madness. The king, in his deep delusions, believed he had to become a dragon himself in order to produce an heir strong enough to link the Flame. His mad plans would find support from Pontiff Sulyvahn, who began experimenting with transforming humans into pale dragons. Despite the large number of failures and abominations that presented only a faded fragment of the dragons' strength, the experiments were eventually successful and Oceiros managed to transform himself into a scaleless dragon resembling Seath, albeit an imperfect and distorted one, even obtaining the sorcery of Seath's crystal breath.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: At some point after Gwyn linked the First Flame and Gwyn's firstborn son was dethroned and exiled, nearly all of the other deities abandoned Anor Londo and moved to an unknown location. Seath remained in his Archives, now completely estranged from the world and obsessed with his research.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Seath's research focused on souls, seeking ways to manipulate them and draw out the power within, mainly through sorcery. Seath, in possession of the Primordial Crystal, noticed the peculiar connection between crystals and souls, and the way in which this element could be used to best catalyze their power, as crystals represented an ideal medium to create a bond between souls and objects. Seath would thus pioneer the Crystal Sorceries, a powerful branch of sorcery. The revelation was the beginning of Seath's obsession with crystals, which became the focus of much of his experiments. He managed to create a Crystal Ember capable of infusing weapons with the power of the crystals and passed this knowledge on to the Giant Blacksmith of the gods.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
His only long range specific attack is the far curse beam. That means if players stay at a distance, one can lure him to fire the beam and charge his defenseless body.

Crystal curse explosion triggers when the player cannot be reached by any of Seath's other attacks; usually when situated behind Seath with the tails just out of reach. One strategy is to begin sprinting a good distance away from him once he arches forward to charge a ball of magic. A second approach would be to develop a high enough curse resistance and block some of the erupting crystals. Immediately heal the damage received before he executes his tail swipes/slams.

Being the grandfather of Sorcery, Seath is extremely resistant to Magic damage, so it would be wise to try to use a different element when combating him.

title: Seath the Scaleless

Gwyn further gifted Seath a fragment of his powerful Lord Soul and the Royal Archives, an enormous library towering above Anor Londo, which contained all the knowledge available to the city of the gods, leaving the dragon the freedom to do his own research; in time, the archives became so synonymous with Seath that they became known as "The Duke's Archives" instead.

snippet:

snippet: At the culmination of his quest, Seath was able to achieve what he had always sought: immortality through the Primordial Crystal. By connecting his body and soul to the powerful crystal, the pale dragon gained insulation from death, so that no mortal blow could affect him and his wounds would close promptly, as long as the crystal was intact. His very breath became a powerful crystal breath that emitted a lethal curse.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
The Japanese description of Seath's Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard uses the Chinese term (Pinyin: *wàiqì*, Hepburn: *gaiseki*) 'consort kin', which is used to define a person related by marriage to the maternal clan or wife's clan of the monarch, indicating that Seath became part of Gwyn's family through marriage with one of the daughters of his mother. However, if interpreted differently by reading the individual kanji separately like 外 (Gai) and 戚 (Seki), it would be translated as "external relative", implying that Seath would have married any woman from Gwyn's family.
**While the term has a historical and cultural meaning too complex to properly convey in the context of the game's lore and the fact that one could become a "Gaiseki" even marrying a sibling or cousin of the monarch's mother or even by having the monarch marry one's daughter, it is more likely that Gwyn gave Seath one of his daughters as a gift, establishing a closer relation between the dragon and the royal family.

The loneliness within him, the bane of his existence since his conception as a malformed dragon, was only fueled by the countless hours wiled away in solitude seeking his "cure"; the void within him was tragically left unfulfilled. The power and status he had since attained remained hollow, against the envy and resentment he harbored first towards his brethren, and then the world at large. His experiments grew more and more twisted as the inescapable reality of his condition drove him insane. snippet: It should not be confused with the Crystal Chime, which can cast Sorceries and Miracles based on leveling Intelligence and Faith equally, or the Izalith Staff, which is designed for Dark Sorceries. title: Archdeacon's Great Staff
snippet:
Archdeacon's Great Staff -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Although it is a staff, the Archdeacon's Great Staff scales purely off of Faith rather than Intelligence. As such, it is designed to be used by builds with high amounts of Faith and utility amounts of Intelligence. Although this requires a high investment in levels into multiple stats, the benefit is that it allows high Faith builds to cast Sorceries with power on par with their Miracles. This allows it to be utilized on very unconventional builds, as both Lightning Stake and Great Heavy Soul Arrow can be cast on the same character to devastating effect.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

While the **Assassin** doesn't have any ranged attack, its Spook Sorcery is extremely useful for removing most non-fatal fall damage and for completely silencing footsteps for 20 seconds, allowing certain obstacles to be bypassed . Unfortunately, while the starting Sorcerer's Staff is a fairly good spell tool, if not exactly the best, it won't actually start to gain scaling from stats until Intelligence has reached at least 19, delaying a possible strengthening of the character's Sorceries.

Picking up the Soul Arrow Sorcery from the Shrine Handmaid gives a reusable ranged attack early on, while the weapon buffing Magic Weapon Sorcery can be gained in either Undead Settlement or Road of Sacrifices to add some of a Staff's spellbuff to weapon damage.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Assassin** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Dexterity-based class with decent Attunement for Weapon Arts and spells and some Intelligence for Sorceries.

An unusually long Thrusting Sword, the Estoc is also quite strong and has a rare sweeping heavy attack for hitting several or agile foes easier, at the cost of not having an increased critical modifier for Ripostes and Backstabs. Additionally, its Weapon Art, Shield Splitter, helps with its bad damage to the stamina of blocking targets by partially bypassing the defences of the block instead.

Its Targeting Shield, while not very suitable for blocking, is one of the game's three parrying shields and as such its Parry starts slightly earlier yet ends as late as the regular parry.

The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This class is fairly popular amongst speedrunners thanks to Spook making it possible to easier skip foes and falls.
While the Assassin doesn't have any direct equivalent class in the Dark Souls series, it does bear some resemblance to the Royalty class from FromSoftware's previous game Demon's Souls, another Dexterity/Intelligence-based class wielding a thrusting sword (in that case a Rapier) and a small shield while also providing access to a Sorcery-like spell (though in the Royalty's case it is the offensive Soul Arrow, not a self-buffing spell).

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bandit (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bandit** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It has high Dexterity and well above average Faith, meaning it lends itself rather well towards builds focused either on both or only the former (though it will have strong competition from the Swordsman when it comes to pure Dexterity builds). It is rather unsuitable to spells, even the Miracle ones, due to its extremely low Attunement and Intelligence.

Bandits are actually unable to speak to Straid of Olaphis by default, the only class that can't do that, due to its extremely low Intelligence not meeting his minimum required amount of 3.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet: There is a curious disadvantage to its high Vitality, higher than any other starting class: when using the Third Dragon Ring, it cannot receive the full benefit of the Flynn's Ring and will get a light decrease of 4 Attack Rating compared to any other class.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Until an unlimited source of arrows is acquired, they are best either saved for trying to pull individual enemies from groups or ambushes, or for trying to kill one of the early Ogres (either the one outside the Firekeeper's Hut in Things Betwixt at the start of the tutorial that also holds the Stone Ring, or the Scholar of the First Sin-exclusive one on the way towards the Forest of Fallen Giants) for a large amount of extra Souls.

The class's Bandit Set is actually fairly good, as it has somewhat high physical defences and is, together with the Knight's partial Falconer Set, the only starting set with decent starting Poise.

Due to its very low Adaptability and Attunement it has a substandard roll (only 7 i-frames, compared to most other classes having 8 or 9 i-frames) and needs 3 points in Adaptability or 9 points in Attunement to improve this to 8 i-frames.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)

The Hand Axe is most likely better replaced with an actually Dexterity-focused weapon, though those are in limited supply until Blacksmith Lenigrast's shop is opened, mostly the Dagger in Things Betwixt and the Halberd in the Forest of Fallen Giants. title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Moonlight Greatsword uses the same moveset as the Greatsword of Judgment, utilizing horizontal and vertical slashes. However, it also has one of the longest reaches among greatswords, being beat only by the Wolf Knight's Greatsword and Onyx Blade. Its skill, Moonlight Vortex, charges the weapon for a powerful thrust attack that channels moonlight energy into a spear-like close-range attack to further augment its lethality. As such, this weapon is best utilized if the wielder equips heavy armor in order to utilize Poise, as is the case with all greatswords in the game.

Fully charging either the one- or two-handed strong attacks will unleash a wave of moonlight energy, at the cost of 4 Durability per use. The moonlight waves inflict only Magic damage; however, hitting an enemy with both the blade and the moonlight wave at close range will result in not only physical damage but also heavy Magic damage being dealt.

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : A time-honored classic returning from the previous *Souls* games, the Moonlight Greatsword is a strong weapon in the hands of a dedicated Sorcery caster.

Unlike its previous iterations, *Dark Souls III*'s Moonlight Greatsword inflicts both physical and Magic damage, as well as being given scaling in Strength, albeit poorly. However, this does not change the fact that the physical scaling should be ignored, outside of meeting the minimum wielding requirements, in favor of leveling Intelligence, as the Moonlight Greatsword has been traditionally built (though as is the case with most melee weapons, it only scales effectively up to 40 in the offensive stats). The physical damage component is useful when performing criticals, as both damage types are magnified during the attack, allowing it to more easily punch through foes' flat Defenses.

 notes : At around 45 Intelligence and onward, the Moonlight Greatsword should be infused with a Faintstone, as the higher scaling bonus begins to overcome the base damage drop.
When infused with a Magic Stone, this weapon's pure Magic damage is replaced by pure Physical damage, and its physical damage reduction goes from 60% to 93.3%, making its block more efficient than most shields against physical attacks. However, this completely nullifies the damage caused by the greatsword's signature strong attack, but the poise damage remains intact.
Due to its relatively low Strength and Dexterity requirements, this weapon is a perfect fit for pure mage builds.

 attributes : Attributes are the base stats of a character. They govern several derived stats and determine which weapons and spells the character can use.

A character's initial attributes depend on the starting class selected by the player during character creation. They can be increased by leveling up the character at the Fire Keeper, or by equipping certain items.

Attribute points gained by leveling up can be redistributed by offering a Pale Tongue to Rosaria in the Cathedral of the Deep.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Hydra -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : The Hydra can be defeated by severing its heads or by targeting the main body and using ranged attacks.

As the player moves closer to the shore, the Hydra will almost exclusively use its head strikes. After it lunges toward the player, each head will bury itself in the ground for a short time, presenting an opportunity to sever its vulnerable necks. As each head is defeated, the spread of the Hydra's attacks will diminish, making it easier for the player to finish the job.

The lunge attacks can be blocked or dodged. Certain spots can be found where the heads will completely miss the player. If the Hydra's position does not change, these spots can be exploited throughout the battle.

title: Undead King Set
snippet:
Undead King Set -  Dark Souls - armor - availability 
 availability : As implied by its name, the Undead King Set was intended to be the boss armor set which would be either sold by Domhnall of Zena, or made available to the player through some other means, upon defeating Undead King Jar-Eel. However, since both it and Jar-Eel were removed from the game, it is unknown how far into the game the player would have been able to purchase it and how much it would have cost.

Due to its nature as cut content, the Undead King Set is simply a texture in the game files. This means that even if the player modified their save file, it would not have its own stats anyway, as an existing armor set's model has to be overridden in order to 'obtain' it. Hence, the armor set can only be seen by those who are modifying the game to use its model.

snippet:

title: Parameter Bonus
snippet:
Parameter Bonus -  Dark Souls - mechanic - stat_rating 
 stat_rating : The stats that improve damage aren't directly used in the calculations; instead, they are first converted to a *rating,* which increases very quickly at low stat levels but slows down after reaching certain "soft caps." All attributes use the same conversion table to determine the bonus they receive from scaling, and Humanity uses its own.

Between each of the data points in the conversion tables, scaling increases linearly. Standard, raw, and crystal weapons, as well as weapons upgraded with twinkling titanite, demon titanite, or dragon scales, use the first table for determining the bonus damage from attributes. Weapons ascended down the Magic, Enchanted, Divine, and Occult paths use the second table for determining bonus damage from attributes.

title: Handmaid's Ladle
snippet:
Handmaid's Ladle -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Handmaiden's Ladle is the weakest weapon in the game, dealing very little damage and featuring no scaling. Its only benefits are its low stat requirements and how early it may be obtained. The only reasons a player may wish to obtain it are:

Having as complete an in-game experience as possible by collecting all the items,
Or for humorous purposes.

While unstated in the item's description, holding the Handmaiden's Ladle in hand increases Vitality and Endurance by one level and Adaptability by two, while decreasing Dexterity by one level.

It can be given some power imbued with Mundane with the correct build. To prevent breaking due to its low durability, wear the Bracing Knuckle Ring or have a stock of Repair Powder. Or ignore the durability, as only 10–20 points of damage are lost when broken.

title: Straight Sword Hilt
snippet:
Straight Sword Hilt -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Straight Sword Hilt can be used to dispatch the harmless Hollows nearby the player's cell as a means to introduce the basic combat mechanics of *Dark Souls*. However, by the time the player makes their first encounter against the Asylum Demon, it will eventually be replaced by their own starting weapons, depending on their class. Only one copy can be obtained per character unless dropped in multi-player.

While useless for the entirety of the game, it is one of two weapons that can be crafted into the true Greatsword of Artorias (the other being the Broken Straight Sword).

If one nevertheless wishes to use it as a standalone weapon, it is best to entirely ignore its nearly non-existent scaling and instead rely on weapon augmentation, with the Sorcery ones (such as Magic Weapon) being the best alternative due to their relatively early availability and reusable nature.

title: Black Dagger
snippet:
Black Dagger -  Dark Souls - weapon - general_information 
 general_information : As it was cut from the final release of the game, it is unknown how the player would have obtained the Black Dagger normally. However, it has been suggested that, because of its similar design to the Darksword of the Darkwraith covenant, it may have been intended to be either an alternate weapon for the Darkwraiths in the New Londo Ruins, or as an additional covenant item given to the player by Darkstalker Kaathe upon ranking up in the Darkwraith covenant.

Due to its nature as cut content, the Black Dagger is simply a texture in the game files. This means that even if the player modified their save file, it would not have its own stats anyway, as an existing weapon's model has to be overridden in order to 'obtain' it. Hence, the weapon can only be seen by those who are modifying the game to use its model.

title: Dreamchaser's Ashes
snippet:
Dreamchaser's Ashes -  Dark Souls III - item - trivia 
 trivia : The icon shows an ashen hand that is clutching what appears to be the Pendant from *Dark Souls*, an item that had no practical use in the game.
**When the Shrine Handmaid is given these ashes, she will ask the Ashen One where they found them. Upon telling her, she will comment how they must have belonged to "one most foolish indeed", perhaps hinting at players trying to figure out the hidden use, which did not actually exist, for the Pendant after Hidetaka Miyazaki, director of *Dark Souls* and *Dark Souls III*, said he'd either choose the Pendant or nothing as his starting gift.

title: Undead Jailer
snippet:
Undead Jailer -  Dark Souls II - enemy - description 
 description : Heavily built hollows wrapped in bandages, and clad in makeshift armor with a cape of what appears to be stitched together hide. Strangely, they can cast Pyromancy without the use of any visible Pyromancy Flame. They wield the Great Machete, cast Fireball in combat, and often have Stray Hounds in tow.

title: Fire Keeper
snippet:
In *Dark Souls II*, the three Fire Keepers in Things Betwixt and the Emerald Herald, believed by some to be Fire Keeper, can be killed without the nearby bonfire being affected. The way the Herald can level up the Bearer of the Curse is reminescent of how the Fire Keepers in *Dark Souls III* can the Ashen One. One of the Keepers, Strowen, offers the player to re-allocate their attributes in exchange for a Soul Vessel.

In *Dark Souls III*, the unnamed Fire Keeper can level up the Ashen One like the Hemerald did in the previous game. She is also immortal; killing her, in addition to not causing the Shrine bonfire to be affected, will only cause her to respawn upon reloading the area, claiming that she cannot die. Instead of a Keeper, it is Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth, the leader of the Rosaria's Fingers covenant, who allows the player to re-allocate their attributes.

title: Rosaria's Fingers
snippet:
**By completing Sirris' questline first and then offering a Pale Tongue to Rosaria, the player can complete both Sirris' and Leonhard's questlines in one NG cycle.
As of Regulation 1.05, players can still reallocate their levels and alter their appearance without gaining hostility from Sirris. However, giving Rosaria a Pale Tongue in order to rank up will make her hostile to the player.
There is a glitch where if the player forces the game to shut down before exiting Rosaria's Dialogue menu after altering appearance or attributes (Such as by shutting off the console), The rebirth will not cost a pale tongue or reduce the remaining rebirth's you have. This is due to the game's auto save function saving your new attributes after a rebirth, but the game not reducing your remaining rebirths or claiming a pale tongue until the dialogue menu is closed. By doing this a player can effectively have infinite rebirths.

title: Ivory Straight Sword
snippet:
Ivory Straight Sword -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Ivory Straight Sword is a very unusual weapon, as it is the only straight sword to deal Strike damage, and each attack consumes ten durability without the use of a Bracing Knuckle Ring. It also has the lowest stability of any weapon in the game, making it inefficient for blocking, and it is considered the second lightest weapon in the game, just behind the Handmaid's Ladle.

One of the other major drawbacks of the Ivory Straight Sword is without a doubt its requirements, as it is necessary to possess points in Dexterity, and the weapon possesses no scaling and cannot be buffed or infused, thus severely limiting its potential in combat. It can, however, be used in conjunction with Flynn's Ring and Ring of Blades, with their full effect, thus augmenting its damage a by a maximum of 100 damage.

title: Symbol of Avarice (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Symbol of Avarice (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - armor - how_to_obtain 
 how_to_obtain : The Symbol of Avarice is a potential drop from all Mimics encountered throughout the course of the game. It may even be obtained from the very first Mimic in the High Wall of Lothric. All Mimics have guaranteed drops, but they may also yield a Symbol of Avarice along with these.

Since Mimics are non-respawning enemies, each encounter with one is very valuable if one is looking to obtain a Symbol of Avarice. The player must first make sure their Item Discovery attribute is as high as possible. Crushing a Rusted Coin, or even a Rusted Gold Coin, before engaging a Mimic is recommended, as well as equipping the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring.

title: White Hair Talisman
snippet:
White Hair Talisman -  Dark Souls III - weapon - how_to_obtain 
 how_to_obtain : In order to survive the trip inside the lava, there are many strategies that can be followed and even combined before venturing inside. The main idea is to slow down the loss of HP enough time, allowing the player to heal up and advance a bit further, repeating the process as many times as necessary until they have successfully gotten the item and returned to solid ground. Each time the player's health reaches half of the HP bar, they should heal.

title: Arbalest
snippet:
Arbalest -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The largest basic crossbow available, the Arbalest is bulky and requires considerable Strength to wield one-handed. Short of the Avelyn however, it is one of the strongest crossbows that can be used in the midst of combat at lock-on range, dealing very respectable damage with each shot.

Care should be taken when wielding this weapon though, as its weight makes it rather unwieldy in situations where it can be fired one-handed. And in situations where it can be two-handed for longer-ranged precision fire, the stats invested in wielding it could be better put to use firing a bow instead, taking advantage of scaling damage.

title: Watcher Greatsword
snippet:
Watcher Greatsword -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Similar to the Defender Greatsword, the Watcher Greatsword's special attack is a unique weapon buff, which is triggered by wielding it in both hands and pressing the Parry button. Rather than a lightning buff, however, the Watcher Greatsword can buff itself with magic.

This buff costs 10 durability each time, meaning it can be used up to five times until breaking. However, the use of the Bracing Knuckle Ring variants reduces the cost of the buff (depending on the level of the ring used), allowing the buff to be used more before breaking the weapon.

In addition to the buff adding magic damage, its fairly low physical stat requirements make it a practical choice for characters with high Intelligence. This, along with its lower weight, stat requirements, faster swing speed, and overall superior scaling makes it a much better choice than the Moonlight Greatsword for high Intelligence builds.

title: Crystal Lizard (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Using a powerful ranged attack can be useful in certain areas where approaching them may be too difficult.
Reloading the game where they spawn can cause them to appear right next to the player. If a lizard managed to escape, all the player has to do is to stand near the spot where the lizard was encountered and exit and continue the game as many times as necessary until the lizard spawns again. This is effective for all lizards in the game, making it possible to slay all of them in places where many can be found gathered together, like The Great Hollow or the Crystal Cave.

title: Eastern Iron Shield
snippet:
Eastern Iron Shield -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : With high physical absorption and very good stability that scales well with upgrades, the Eastern Iron Shield is best thought of as a pocket Medium Shield. Boasting the highest physical resistance of all Small Shields in the game, it can be used to reliably ward off physical attacks, though at the cost of tying for the second-heaviest Small Shield in the game, and lacking the ability to parry incoming attacks.

Due to its ability to use the skill of the right-hand weapon, it is best utilized on offensive builds that are lacking in the Vitality or Strength to equip a heavier shield.

title: Mimic (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
A Mimic is easily recognizable by the extended chain that lies on its side. Conversely, if the chain is curved backward, then it means the chest is real and can be safely looted.

There are two variants:
The *Dark Souls* variant, and the most commonly seen, is the standing one, where the Mimic will engage in melee-combat by performing punches and kicks, occasionally attempting to grab and chew on the player.
The *Dark Souls II* variant, where the Mimic will first turn around and drop on its back, crawling in a backward position on its four limbs in a manner similar to a spider.

Mimics are non-respawning enemies and each one has a specific guaranteed drop, these always being a rare or unique item. In addition, all Mimics encountered in the game have a chance of dropping a Symbol of Avarice, a unique head armor that grants extra souls acquisition and boosts Item Discovery at the cost of draining HP while worn.

title: Giant Stone Axe
snippet: The unupgraded Giant Stone Axe is an extremely underwhelming weapon, with low base damage and scaling, but it quickly improves as it is upgraded. This, combined with its various drawbacks, makes the Giant Stone Axe far less accessible in the early game than it might initially seem. While this can be circumvented through careful stat allocation and knowing how to obtain the required materials, it may be prudent to save the weapon for later into a playthrough when its requirements are less cumbersome. For more accessible early game Greataxes, players may want to consider the standard Greataxe, or the unorthodox Bandit Greataxe, as a bridging weapon until later.

title: Bastard Sword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Bastard Sword (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : A ubiquitous weapon, the Bastard Sword is a very economical greatsword that makes it strong on a number of builds.

At 8.0 units, the Bastard Sword is the third-lightest greatsword in the game, beat by the Drakeblood Greatsword and Wolnir's Holy Sword and tying with the Storm Ruler. As well, it has virtually no Dexterity requirements to wield, allowing almost any build to equip and use it. And finally, its stamina consumption is among the lowest among all greatswords in the game, granting its wielder improved stamina economy.

The Bastard Sword specializes in horizontal and vertical slashing attacks. It has a similar moveset to the Claymore, though it lacks the latter's thrusting attacks, which limits its reach and makes it difficult to use in corridors.

title: Fume Ultra Greatsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
However, it is the heaviest ultra greatsword in the game, and it also requires the greatest amount of Strength to wield of any ultra greatsword. As well, swinging the weapon consumes copious amounts of stamina, more than other ultra greatswords, and none of its thrusting attacks actually deal Thrust damage, preventing it from benefiting from counter-attacks. Due to its immense weight, it is crucial that the player invest not only in Strength, but also invest heavily into Endurance and Vitality.

Despite requiring Twinkling Titanite to upgrade, the Fume Ultra Greatsword can still be buffed. This means that its monstrous damage output can be further augmented with the use of buffs and resins, giving it the ability to add elemental damage that a foe is weak to, or to chip through enemies who are relying heavily on shields.

title: Pyromancer
snippet:
Pyromancers do, however, start with the worst shield in the game, although it is still reasonably effective up until the point where a player can obtain a better one.

The basic pyromancy trainer, Laurentius of the Great Swamp, is one of the last trainers available to the player. Therefore, pyromancers have access to no pyromancies other than Fireball until this point, that is; without the Master Key which allows anyone access to Quelana of Izalith who teaches expert level pyromancies, and Eingyi who has a secret Pyromancy Flame and toxic spells.

The stat distribution for Pyromancers makes them more optimal than Sorcerers for Intelligence builds in most cases, being able to use Moonlight Butterfly Horn at base stats. One can start as Pyromancer, rescue Griggs of Vinheim as soon as possible, and gear up as a mage.

title: Titanite Demon
snippet:
A somewhat reliable melee approach is to position oneself behind its left arm, where it appears to be missing a leg. Its close-range attacks will miss, letting the player hit once or twice. Its tail can still inflict minor damage, as it swings along with its weapon. However, the demon will perform a jump attack if the player remains in this spot, or behind it, for too long.
Alternatively, staying under its left arm will cause most of its attacks to swing harmlessly overhead if the player is far right enough or low enough during their attack animations. This does not trigger its jump attack. Its second combo attack can be more easily avoided if the player moves to its center by the leg, but then, the third pole jab in its attack pattern needs the player to move back near its arm to avoid damage.
The pole-grab can be dodged by moving behind its right leg or left arm, allowing a counterattack.

title: Warlock Mask
snippet:
Warlock Mask -  Dark Souls II - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Warlock Mask is arguably one of the best head armors in the entire game. When fully upgraded and worn with the required Intelligence, it possesses the following traits:
Increases Intelligence by 2 points.
**This increase affects weapon and armor requirements, and therefore reduces the actual requirement to wear the mask to 12 Intelligence.
Increases number of Souls acquired by 2.5% (same value as the Tseldora Cap, Nahr Alma Hood or Symbol of Avarice).
Best Dark Defense in the game for headgear (72 points).
Best Magic Defense in the game for headgear (72 points).
Best Petrification Resist in the game for headgear (47 points).
2nd best Curse Resist in the game for headgear (120 points, which is only 5 points less than the Xanthous Crown).
2nd best Lightning Defense in the game for headgear (48 points, which is only 3 points less than the Archdrake Helm).

title: Dark Souls II
snippet:
Dark Souls II -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - gameplay 
 gameplay : Similar to the previous title, players customize the gender and physical features of their character, in addition to choosing a starting class, which determines the stats and equipment that the player begins with, and a starting gift. From a third-person perspective, players explore a continuous, open world that is roughly the same size as the original game, but with more freedom in how the player can progress. Akin to the notorious difficulty of its predecessor, players are confronted by a persistently hostile environment with unrelenting enemies and bosses – death is a central theme. As enemies are defeated, souls are accumulated, acting as both a form of currency and means to increase attributes. Unlike the first game, however, the player can have a voice chat with other players in their world.

title: Great Machete (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Great Machete (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Great Machete provides one of the earliest accesses to heavy weaponry in the game, should the player is lucky enough to obtain one as a drop from a Hollow Manservant while traversing the Undead Settlement.

While its 24 Strength requirement will have the player investing frequently in this attribute, the rewards are well worth the effort, since the force with which each swing with this weapon is performed will kill most enemies in only one or two hits, making it also a good choice for spending the first upgrade materials obtained on it.

It has the basic greataxe moveset and also has decent reach.

Its skill, "Sharpen", boosts the weapon's attack rating by 10%.

title: Great Scythe (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Great Scythe (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Great Scythe is the archetype of its weapon class, a long-reaching polearm which can damage targets through raised shields.

Found early in the game, the Great Scythe's attributes make it attractive to builds that specialize in Dexterity. It is also the lightest reaper in the game, allowing builds with low Vitality to wield it with few problems. As with other polearms, it possesses a sweet-spot mechanic where hitting a target with the blade of the weapon will inflict full Slash damage, but if the target is inside of the weapon's arc it will inflict reduced damage and deal Strike damage instead.

title: Drakewing Ultra Greatsword
snippet:
Drakewing Ultra Greatsword -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : A sword decorated with drake wings. Use strong attack to unleash its latent power.

The blade of this sword is split into two, and is best swung in smashing motions rather than slices.

Drakes are likely descendants of the ancient dragons, and although their strength pales in comparison to the what is described in legend, to mere humans they are still mighty beasts.

title: Elite Knight Set (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Elite Knight Set (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : The set boasts one of the highest defense/weight ratios in the game, with stats comparable to that of Havel's Set or the Stone Set when fully upgraded, while weighing nowhere near as much. On the other hand, the Elite Knight set features generally unremarkable Poise. As this set can be acquired relatively early in the game, it stands as a viable choice for low-mid level characters to rely on straight out of the box, and potentially throughout the entirety of the game with frequent upgrading. Due to its low weight compared to much heavier sets with similar defenses that are much more costly to upgrade, a high level player could be able to obtain full mobility despite the weight, resulting in much more effective combat with both defense and agility.

title: Darkeater Midir
snippet:
The water in Midir's arena has a similar aesthetic to the sludge in Aldrich's, having various bones and pieces of flesh floating in it. Those corpses will bleed if struck with any weapon.
The water itself is able to be seen through, it looks as though the pool is deep, as one can see the supposed floor beneath it, meaning the player would be walking on the surface of the water itself.
The transition attack where Midir breathes fire and then blasts his dark beam may be an homage to *Shin Godzilla*, a fictional film monster.
The sorcery born from his soul, Old Moonlight, is possibly a nod to the earlier designs of the Moonlight Greatsword, as seen in Demon's Souls.
During his Abyssal flame breath attacks, it is possible to hear what resembles a human chorus amidst Midir's inferno. It is most audible at the encounter on the bridge, as there is no soundtrack and little ambient noise during this battle.
